title: Insight 1: Aug 12 ride touched Z2 ceiling
description: Your August 12 ride averaged 159 bpm, exactly at the top of your Z2 range (139–159 bpm). Keeping easy rides a few beats lower (around 155 bpm) will build aerobic fitness with less fatigue.

title: Insight 2: Aug 23 long ride vertical load high
description: The 81 km ride on August 23 had 452 m of climbing, nearly double the elevation of your other rides (200–330 m). That extra vertical load adds leg fatigue—enjoy the hills but allow an extra recovery day after big climbing days.

title: Insight 3: Three rides in a week flags density
description: You rode three times in the last seven days (Aug 21, 23, 27) with a 3‑hour ride sandwiched between two shorter ones. This density is fine for now, but avoid adding a fourth ride until readiness stays above 75.

title: Insight 4: Cycling progression solid
description: Your longest ride grew from 35 km (Aug 19) to 81 km (Aug 23) in two weeks—a great progression. Celebrate the distance gains, but keep weekly increases under 15% to stay happy and injury‑free.

title: Insight 5: Power zones need recalibration
description: Your power zones still use an FTP of 271 W from March 2025, but recent 20‑minute bests are only 143–204 W. A realistic FTP is likely 150–195 W—update your zones so easy rides stay truly easy.

title: Insight 6: Polarized 80/20 balance good
description: About 80% of your ride time sits in Z2 (139–159 bpm), with only brief touches of Z3. That’s a great polarized balance for joyful improvement—keep the easy days easy and the hard days fun.

title: Insight 7: Recovery warning signs
description: Readiness dipped to 58 on August 24 after only 5h 53m sleep, and HRV dropped to 65. Prioritize 7+ hours sleep and consider a very easy spin or rest day when readiness falls below 65.

title: Insight 8: Sprint power shows leg speed
description: Your 10‑second sprint power hit 439 W on August 21, showing good leg snap. If you enjoy sprints, add a few 10‑second all‑out efforts once a week to keep that reactivity without overdoing it.

title: Insight 9: VO2max interval suggestion
description: To boost VO2max, try a fun session: warm up, then 3 × 4 minutes at 167–175 bpm (Z4–Z5) with 4 minutes easy spinning between. Do this once a week on a fresh day for a happy fitness lift.

title: Insight 10: FTP estimate from 20‑min best
description: Your best 20‑minute power across recent rides is 160 W (Aug 23). A simple FTP estimate is 95% of that: ~152 W. Use 150–155 W for setting power zones until you do a proper test.
